title: Combined effects of particle geometry and applied vibrations on the mechanics and strength of entangled materials
access: Author institution PDF; page 10 Figures 10 and 11 rendered and inspected
evidence: In the DEM analysis, a steady mean entanglement can coexist with nonzero entangling and disentangling rates. Steel-staple experiments show jagged tensile curves and history dependence.
scope: Previously used in cycle 39 for vibration and confinement. Here it motivates tracking reformation during slip; no force, rate or geometry parameter transferred to warm polymer particles.
data_access: Underlying data available from corresponding author on reasonable request; no data request sent and no raw-data reproduction claimed.

title: Tuning geometry in staple-like entangled particles: pick-up experiments and Monte Carlo simulations
authors: Youhan Sohn; Saeed Pezeshki; Francois Barthelat
evidence: Pick-up efficacy depends on leg angle, length and backbone thickness. The geometry that maximizes lifted fraction need not maximize short-distance release.
scope: Steel and acrylic staples at low-rate laboratory conditions; not a snow ski test. Neither optimal angle nor lifted fraction is adopted as a success probability or material property.

title: Transient response of nonlinear polymer networks: A kinetic theory
evidence: Population kinetics distinguish deformation, attachment in a relaxed configuration and detachment of loaded chains, with stress and energy depending on the distribution.
scope: Methodological analogy only. This cycle uses discrete particle-contact proxies, not a calibrated molecular network or reproduction of the paper's nonlinear polymer law.
